newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Waves drown six revellers in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Waves drown six revellers in Philippines.

text.p: Six people on a pleasure cruise drowned on Sunday when heavy waves overturned their boat as rains pounded a wide area of the Philippines, triggering floods and volcanic mudflows, police said.

They said 11 occupants of the boat were rescued while one was missing after their vessel sank off central Cebu island. They were having a picnic to celebrate the passing by three of them of state examinations for licenses to practice law, police said.

Heavy rains induced by a tropical depression flooded parts of Manila and triggered five-foot (1.5-metre) high mudflows from nearby Mount Pinatubo volcano, but there were no reports of casualties, relief officials said.

The mudflows, confined to river channels, consisted of tonnes of rocks and volcanic ash deposited on the slopes of Pinatubo when it erupted in 1991 in one of the century's biggest volcanic blasts. More than 800 people died in the wake of the eruption, mostly refugees who succumbed to diseases in evacuation camps.
